svg.text: claudia — styling suite 2.1: cells take styles as paragraphs do (computes)
Proposal for review. A cell has one style, named by what it is for (D311, D313); the grid draws it, the toolbar and the Format menu apply it.
A · A small price model, styled by purpose
Header, Input, Result and Note are the built-ins; column E carries Input as a whole column.
Column E is empty but styled as a whole column: the grid paints it without a cell element per row, down to row 1 048 576.
B · Format ▸ Apply style ▸ with cells selected
The agreed menu (format-menu-apply-style.svg), offering what fits a cell.
With a floating object selected instead, the same menu offers what fits
that object's slot (its outline, or its words) — one menu, the host
(Flyout drawn below the menu here for room; in the app it opens to the side.)
The quick list sits at the right end of the formula-bar row, as composes' style list sits in its toolbar: it shows the active cell's style and applies to the whole selection. Each entry is
drawn in its look (font, weight, italics, colour, background chip; never the size).
Applying a style fills both slots of each selected cell (D311): Input gives the box its pale background and the words their accent colour. Typing into a cell never changes its style; there
A whole column, a whole row or the whole sheet takes a style the same way, by selecting its header. The last action wins (D317): every cell of the column gets the style, those styled before
too, and so do its empty cells and the ones typed into later.
“Clear cell style” takes the selected cells' own style away, so the row's, column's or sheet's style (or Body text) shows through again. It is the one entry this menu has that composes' has
Number formats (€, thousands) are not styles and are not in this menu (D75).
